As soon as he married she automatically comes to the caste of her husband i.e., accused No.1.
Thereby provisions of - 11 - C/W Section 3(2) (v) of SC/ST(PA) Act would not attract and the learned Sessions Judge is not justified in convicting the accused No.1 under the provisions of Section 3(2) (v) of SC/ST(PA) Act,
that too after the amendment of provisions of the Act.
Non examination creates suspicion and credibility of the evidence of PWs-9 to 11, thereby the judgment of conviction is bad in law.
Alternatively, he further contend that on the date of the incident on 16.10.2014,
when he was along with PW-9 and deceased, an accidental fire occurred and there was no intention to kill his own wife as he had love and got married and registered, thereby the provisions of Section 302 I.P.C would not attract, utmost provisions of Section 304 would attract, in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances and the said aspect of the matter has not been considered by learned Sessions Judge while convicting the accused under the provisions of Section - 14 - C/W 498A and 302 I.P.C.

The learned Sessions Judge proceeded to convict Accused No.1 under the - 31 - C/W provisions of Section 3(2)(v) of the SC & ST (POA) though only general allegations made in the complaint as well as in the evidence of PWs.9,10, 11 and 12.
Admittedly, the deceased married the accused No.1 on 28.1.2014 and therefore, question of invoking the provisions of Section 3(2(v) of the SC & ST (PA) Act against the Accused No.1 would not arise.
Apart from that, the incident happened on 16.10.2014 and the amendment to the Section 3(2)(v) of the SC & ST (PA) Act came into force in the year 2016, thereby the said provision is not attracted.
The learned Sessions Judge without considering the said material facts of the case, has convicted Accused NO.1 for the offence punishable under Section 3(2)(v) of the SC & ST (PA) Act merely because the deceased Sunitha belonged to Scheduled Tribe, ignoring the fact that the accused No.1 and the deceased married and question of insulting and abusing such words with wife does not arise.
In the entire evidence of the prosecution witnesses and in the material documents, there is no whisper with regard to Accused Nos.2 to 4 assaulting and insulting the deceased.
As admitted by PW.10 and PW.9 - 32 - C/W in their evidence, in order to facilitate Accused No.1 and the deceased, PW.10 arranged separate house for the accused No.1 and the deceased.
As on the date of the incident, Accused No.1,
deceased and PW.9 were in the house.
The very inclusion of the provisions of SC & ST (PA) Act by the Investigating Officer is without any basis.
To invoke the said provision, the offence must have been committed against the person on the ground such person is a member of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
There is no evidence to show that the offence committed only on the ground that the victim or the deceased was a member of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
Therefore,
in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the impugned judgment of conviction passed by the trial Court in so far as convicting and sentencing accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 3(2)(v) of SC & ST (PA) Act, cannot be sustained and the same is liable to be set aside.
18. Therefore, offence under the Act is not established merely on the fact that the informant is a member of Scheduled Caste unless there is an intention to humiliate a member of Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe for the reason that the victim belongs to such caste.
In the present case, the parties are litigating over possession of the land.
The allegation of hurling of abuses is against a person who claims title over the property.
If such person happens to be a Scheduled Caste, the offence under Section 3(1)(r) of the Act is not made out.
Even the complaint/Ex.P21 clearly depicts that only the Accused No.1 abused and poured kerosene and lit the fire to the deceased.
